findings.oracle: Real disk-loaded HexDocument (256-byte identity file); oracle is the hand-enumerated identity constant bytes([0x7E,0x7F,0x80,0x81]) cross-checked against bytes(range(126,130)) plus the 0xFD/0xFE/0xFF tail, and a new TestFixtureIntegrity class independently proves the fixture is the value==offset identity sequence via read_byte(i)==i for all 256 offsets; corrupting the native read turns the exact-byte asserts red.

Real in-memory HexDocument from open_bytes; pre-write asserts pin neighbors at identity constants bytes([48..53]) (not sample_bytes), write 0xAA/0xBB at offset 50 which differs from identity 0x32/0x33, then assert exact post-write bytes and that offsets 48-49/52-53 stay at identity values; TestFixtureIntegrity independently verifies the fixture, so a no-op write, a write bleeding past range, or a corrupt fixture all fail.
